The present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with interest for the death of Sri. Nagarajappa @ Nagarajappa B.N. @ Bandi Nagarajappa in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 27.09.2022.
2.

The case of petitioners in brief is as under:
That, on 27.09.2022 at about 5.00 p.m., while deceased SCCH-10 Nagarajappa was walking on left side foot path of Pipeline Road, in front of Magnum International school, T. Dasarahalli, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of Pulsar Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JF-1879 suddenly came from Malasandra towards Ayyappa Temple road with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said Nagarajappa and
Due to the accident he sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to N.R.R. hospital, Hesaraghatta Main road, Bengaluru and after first aid he was shifted to K.C. General hospital, Malleshwaram, wherein he took inpatient treatment from 28.09.2022 to 03.10.2022 and under went surgery and after discharge he was taking outpatient treatment.
Further, on 31.10.2022 due to left leg swelling again he was admitted to said K.C. General hospital and took treatment from 31.10.2022 to 06.11.2022.

During this period, the Peenya Traffic police have registered FIR in crime No.196/2022 for the offence u/s 279 and 338 of IPC and then filed charge sheet against the rider of offending motor cycle for the offence u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
However, said Nagarajappa succumbed to the fatal SCCH-10 injuries on 19.01.2023.
The petitioners have spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment including last rites and funeral expenses.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons of the deceased.

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, he was doing fruit selling business and was earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
Due to death of deceased, the petitioners are put to mental shock and agony and also lost their bread earner of the family.

Further, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Bajaj Pulsar Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-JF- 1879.
As such, the respondent No.1 being insurer and respondent No.2 being owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petition.
3. In response to the Petition notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.

The respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court,
remained absent and placed exparte.
SCCH-10 4
. The brief contentions of the respondent No.1 in the objection statement are as under:
The respondent No.1 contended that, the claim petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable.

The respondent No.1 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JF-1879 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident, however the liability if any subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

The respondent No.1 has denied the accident,
manner in which the accident took place and rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending Motor cycle and also denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Further denied the medical expenses incurred by the petitioners.
Further contended that, the rider of the motor cycle was intoxicated at the time of alleged accident and hence there is a violation of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further denied the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
It is contended that, there is no nexus between the alleged SCCH-10 accident, the injuries sustained and death.
As per the police records, death of deceased is not due to the alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and fanciful.
On these grounds, respondent No.1 prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Nagarajappa died in the accident that occurred on 27.08.2022 at about 5.00 p.m., on Pipeline Road, opp; Magnum International School, T. Dasarahalli, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent riding of the Pulsar Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JF-1879 ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?

Sharadhamma vs Kotak Mahindra Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147660230/
3 3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?

If so, at what amount and from whom?
4) What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.3 examined himself as PW-1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to SCCH-10 Ex.P.16.
The petitioners also examined MRD of K.C. General hospital as PW-2 and got marked documents as Ex.P.17 and Ex.P.18.

The respondent No.1 has examined its Deputy Manager Legal as RW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
7.
Heard arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

8. My finding to the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Negative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S 9. ISSUE No.1:

The petitioners have filed the present claim petition seeking compensation on account of death of Sri. Nagarajappa @ Nagarajappa B.N. @ Bandi Nagarajappa in a road traffic accident that occurred on 27-09-2022.
To substantiate their case, son of the deceased i.e. the petitioner No.3 examined himself as PW-1 and in all got SCCH-10 marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.
Ex.P.1 is the FIR No.0196/2022 of Peenya Traffic PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that, I.O. has registered a case against the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-JF-1879 for the commission of offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.

Ex.P.3 is the charge sheet filed by the Peenya Traffic police for the offence punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC against one Mr. Bharath Booshan. M.S., who is none other than the rider of the offending motor cycle.
Ex . P.7

is the wound certificate issued by N.R.R.
hospital, wherein it reveals that, Nagarajappa has sustained fractures of both bones of left leg and contusion on the right side forehead.

Ex. P.8 and Ex.P.15 are the discharge summaries wherein it reveal that, said Nagarajappa admitted to K.C. General hospital, Malleshwaram on 28.09.2022 and discharged on 03.10.2022 and once again he was admitted to the said hospital on 31.10.2022 and discharged on 06.11.2022.
Ex.P.16 is the death certificate of said Nagarajappa wherein it reveals that, Nagarajappa died on 19.01.2023 i.e. after 113 SCCH-10 days from the date of accident.

The FIR was registered on 28.09.2022 and charge sheet was filed by the police on 15.10.2022.
10.
According to the petitioners, the death was on account of injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

On the contrary, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has vehemently argued that,
there is no nexus between the injury and death of the deceased and there is no proof to establish that the death was caused on account of the injuries sustained in the alleged accident.

Admittedly, in the instant case after the death of the deceased, no post mortem was done to assess the cause of Sharadhamma vs Kotak Mahindra Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147660230/
4 death.

sentences.text: Further, the petitioners have not reported the death of said Nagarajappa to the concerned police and the police have also not investigated the case and no additional charge sheet or investigation report were filed by the police to show that the death was caused due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
As stated supra, said Nagarajappa has sustained injury only on the left leg and there is no other serious SCCH-10 injuries sustained in the alleged accident.
It cannot be believed that the injury on the left leg will cause death of a person.
In the instant case, the deceased was aged more than 70 years on the date of accident.

Considering the gap between the date of accident and the date of death, non availability of post mortem report as well as additional charge sheet, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, though said Nagarajappa has suffered injuries in the road traffic accident and the accident caused due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle, there is no nexus between the injury and cause of death of said Nagarajappa.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have failed to establish that the death was caused on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is answered in the Negative.
11. ISSUE No.2:-

It is the contention of the petitioners that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, the petitioner No.2 and 3 are the SCCH-10 sons of the deceased Sri. Nagarajappa @
Nagarajappa B.N. @ Bandi Nagarajappa and they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased.

The petitioner No.3 in his chief examination affidavit has stated that,
the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and himself are the sons of deceased Nagarajappa.

Since the respondents have not much disputed the relationship between the petitioners, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioner No.1 to 3 are the legal heirs and the dependents of the deceased.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE No.3:
As discussed supra, in the instant case the petitioners have failed to establish the nexus between the injury and cause of death of said Nagarajappa.

Therefore, the petitioners are not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency,
loss of consortium, loss of estate and towards funeral expenses.

13. According to the petitioners, immediately after the accident said Nagarajappa was shifted to N.R.R. hospital SCCH-10 and after first aid he was shifted to K.C. General hospital, Malleshwaram,
wherein he took inpatient treatment from 28.09.2022 to 03.10.2022 and under went surgery and after discharge he was taking outpatient treatment.
Further, on 31.10.2022 due to left leg swelling again he was admitted to said K.C. General hospital and took treatment from 31.10.2022 to 06.11.2022.
Ex.P.9 and Ex.P.10 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.30,336/- and the medical prescriptions are marked as Ex.P.11.
On perusal of the injury sustained by said Nagarajappa, it appears that the petitioners might have spent more than Rs.30,000/- towards medical and other incidental charges.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, in addition to the medical expenses as well as nourishment and died food and also hospital expenses, if Global compensation Sharadhamma vs Kotak Mahindra Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147660230/
5 of Rs.50,000/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As far as liability is concerned, respondent No.1 insurance company has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and same was in force as on the date of SCCH-10 accident.

Therefore,
the respondent No.1/insurer is liable to pay Global compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. to the petitioners from the date of petition till its realization in the ratio of 50:25:25 respectively.
Accordingly, I answer the Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.4:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total Global compensation of Rs.50,000/-
with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. at the ratio of 50:25:25 respectively from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.

The respondent No.1 insurance company is liable to pay compensation amount as awarded to the petitioners and directed to deposit the SCCH-10 compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The entire amount awarded to petitioners shall be released in their respective names through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- Draw award accordingly.
